Definition: a primary root; to lift up; by implication, to take up or away; figuratively, to raise (the voice), keep in suspense (the mind), specially, to sail away (i.e. weigh anchor); by Hebraism (compare H5375) to expiate sin:--away with, bear (up), carry, lift up, loose, make to doubt, put away, remove, take (away, up).
BiblicalUsage: The word does heavy work all through the Gospels. The devil quotes Psalm 91 to Jesus — the angels will bear thee up in their hands; John the Baptist points at Jesus and says, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world; the crowd takes up stones to kill Him; and Jesus tells anyone who will follow Him to take up his cross. Lift, bear, carry away, remove — one verb, and the cross gathers all its meanings.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heart of this word is John 1:29: He takes away sin the way a servant carries a burden off someone else's back. And the call is the same shape in reverse — we take up our cross and follow the One who took up ours.
RelatedEvents: The Temptation in the Wilderness; The Baptism of Jesus
